summary.title: Baking Pi – Operating Systems Development
summary.one_liner: A lesson-based course that teaches basic operating system development in ARM assembly on the Raspberry Pi, from blinking the activity LED to building a simple command line interface.
keywords: how do i write an operating system
takeaways: Set up a cross-compiler on a separate development computer and deploy the built kernel to a Raspberry Pi SD card.
Control the OK/ACT LED with assembly, then use functions and the system timer to flash it at precise intervals and produce an SOS pattern.
Draw graphics on screen: gradients, lines, pseudo-random numbers and text, plus reading the kernel command line.
Handle keyboard input through a basic driver and build a simple command line interface for an OS.
summary.summary: The course is a series of lessons, each with theory and a practical exercise with a full answer, taken in order. It starts with an introduction and an LED series (OK01 to OK05), moves to a screen series covering graphics, lines, text and computed values (Screen01 to Screen04), and ends with an input series on drivers, keyboard input and a command line interface (Input01 and Input02). The author assumes no prior OS or assembly knowledge, though some programming experience helps. The page notes that the course has not been updated for the Raspberry Pi B+, A+ or v2 models, so some early LED lessons may not work.
